observations: Four corded rotary hammer drills lying on a dirt/sandy surface.
The brand 'ozito' is clearly visible on the side of the tools in photo 0.
The tools feature a grey body with red accents and selector switches.
One unit has a sticker visible in photo 0 labeled '3 MODE' with 'HAMMER', 'DRILL', and 'CHISEL' icons.
The tools appear used, with visible dust and surface wear.
Power cords are present, but the plugs are not clearly shown.

claims.evidence: photo 0 shows the Ozito brand name on the tools.

claims.claim: for drilling, punching and chiseling of concrete
claims.evidence: photo 0 shows a 3-mode selector sticker including a chisel function.

risks.risk: The motor may be burnt out, weak, or non-functional.
risks.proof: A video of the drill running and successfully drilling into a concrete block.

risks.risk: The SDS chuck mechanism may be worn out and unable to hold bits securely.
risks.proof: A video showing a bit being inserted, locked, and used under load.

risks.risk: The internal hammer/piston mechanism may be failed despite the motor spinning.
risks.proof: A video demonstrating the tool in hammer-only (chiseling) mode.
risks.if_unproven: as a standard rotary drill only

risks.risk: The power cord may have internal breaks or dangerous exposed wiring.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the full length of the cord and the plug.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the specification plate on the side of the tool to identify the model number and wattage.
Video of the tool being powered on and tested in all three modes (drill, hammer-drill, chisel).
Photo of the power plug to confirm it matches local sockets.
response.reason: The specific model number and power rating (wattage) are not legible in the photo, and these details significantly determine the value of power tools. Additionally, the functional condition of the motor and hammer mechanism cannot be verified from a still image.
